questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Scaled Random Variable
questions.worked_solution:
For any constant $a$ and any random variable $X,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[aX]=a\text{E}[X].
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-8X] & =-8\text{E}[X] \\  & =(-8)(0.5) \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Scaled Random Variable
questions.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.74$ | $0.07$ | $0.08$ | $0.09$ | $0.02$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[0.5X].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.74+1\cdot 0.07+2\cdot 0.08+3\cdot 0.09+4\cdot 0.02 \\  & =0.58.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[0.5X] & =0.5\text{E}[X] \\  & =0.5\cdot 0.58 \\  & =0.29.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[-0.25X].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot 0.3+2\cdot 0.1+4\cdot 0.1+6\cdot 0.3+8\cdot 0.2 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-0.25X] & =-0.25\text{E}[X] \\  & =-0.25\cdot 4 \\  & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Transformed Random Variable
questions.worked_solution:
For any constants $a$ and $b$ and any random variable $X,$ we have

$$
\text{E}[aX+b]=a\text{E}[X]+b.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[-6X-1] & =-6\text{E}[X]-1 \\  & =-6(-\frac{3}{2})-1 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Expected Value of a Transformed Random Variable
questions.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.15$ | $0.1$ | $0.15$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[3-10X].$
questions.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =-4\cdot 0.15-2\cdot 0.1+0\cdot 0.15+1\cdot 0.35+2\cdot 0.25 \\  & =0.05.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[3-10X] & =\text{E}[-10X+3] \\  & =-10\text{E}[X]+3 \\  & =-10\cdot 0.05+3 \\  & =2.5.\end{aligned}
$$
